She was super personable and really funny, and knew a lot about the products. The atmos

farmersmarket.name: Barossa Farmers Market
reviews: If you have a couple of hours to kill and want to experience the local produce and vibrant atmosphere. There are live music, coffee and foods served on site. Beautiful fresh veggies, pastries, artisan breads you name it so. Highly recommended.

A lovely little weekend market with a good selection of local produce and products as well as some nice food and drink options. A great way to start a Saturday and see what's available from the region.
Excellent variety of vendors with tasty and unique products, plenty of locals and tourists and fabulously priced fresh produce. Loads of cars, busy market.
So much lovely produce! And everyone was so nice! Absolutely loved it. Went back to the motel with lots and lots of goodies!

greenockbrewers.name: Greenock Brewers Barossa Valley
reviews: Sensational local brewery with a great range, especially fine pale ale. Chris and his partner have created an outstanding venue with a fabulous offering and a real passion for warm hospitality and great hospitality. Ask Chris to explain how his products are unique:-). Donât miss going here if you

7 star review. This is a hidden gem!!!! Amazing service from what I presume was the owner, great beer and exceptional venue. As a result of our brief stop here we will be coming back and staying a weekend in the caravan park.

Owner was so lovely. Explained all the local beers and made us feel like we already knew him, not a tourist. Even gave us a map and directions to another brewery in the area. If we had more time, we'd spend our day there. And we are definitely going back. Beers were so tasty!

Wow, what an awesome place. Beers are magnificent and Chris ( the owner, brewer, barman) is really knows his stuff. I tried all beers and couldn't fault any. Great to see someone who is so passionate about his business. Nice Sunday arvo to chill and chat with locals.

reviews: Perched on Menglers Hill, this open-air gallery was created in the early 2000s by local artist Franz Keml, turning the landscape into a space where art, nature, and community come together. The sculptures reflect themes of creativity, resilience, and connection to the land, making the park feel both

Menglers Hill Lookout is certainly worth a visit to get a great view down across the Barossa - plus its where you can explore the Barossa Sculpture Park with its quirky sculptures and a nice walk. Plus there is the Pioneer Memorial commemorating the Lutheran migrant pioneers of Barossa. In 1840s the
Fun place to go for sundown. The sculptures are unremarkable, but it's a great view from the lookout point, and on a clear day you can see the sun set over the ocean.
Ok if you're into sculpture. Large works of art that must have taken ages to complete but too inspiring.
